newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkey, north Cyprus sign economic protocol.
newsitem.headline: Turkey, north Cyprus sign economic protocol.

text.p: Turkey and the breakaway northern Cyprus republic signed a protocol on Saturday to boost economic relations and help the northern part of the divided island overcome economic bottlenecks, officials said.
They said the prime ministers of the north Cyprus government, recognised only by Ankara, and of Turkey would sign an agreement soon to implement the protocol.
Inal Batu, the Turkish foreign ministry official who signed the protocol, said it would "broaden and deepen economic cooperation by providing credits for projects and joint ventures" in north Cyprus.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974, when Turkish troops occupied the northern third of the island in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup engineered by a junta then ruling in Greece.

Officials said the protocol would also help close public deficits of the northern government but declined to give any figures. The north Cyprus economy has been in the doldrums with annual inflation running over 100 percent.
Officials denied the protocol was a step to "an economic integration with Turkey".
